description_full: Bank First Corporation operates as a holding company for Bank First, N.A. that provides consumer and commercial financial services to businesses, professionals, and consumers, in Wisconsin. It offers checking, savings, money market, cash management, retirement, and health savings accounts; other time deposits; certificates of deposit; and residential mortgage products. The company also provides loan products include real estate loans, including commercial real estate, residential mortgage, and home equity loans; commercial and industrial loans for working capital, accounts receivable, inventory financing, and other business purposes; construction and development loans; residential 1-4 family loans; and consumer loans for personal and household purposes, including secured and unsecured installment loans, and revolving lines of credit. In addition, it provides credit cards; insurance; data processing and other information technology; investment and safekeeping; treasury management; and online, telephone, and mobile banking services. The company was formerly known as Bank First National Corporation and changed its name to Bank First Corporation in June 2019. Bank First Corporation was founded in 1894 and is headquartered in Manitowoc, Wisconsin.

financial_summary: Bank First Corporation is a small-cap financial services business with a $1.7B market cap on $174M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +12% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 21% against a 8% cost of capital — a 13-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $51M in free cash flow — roughly 29 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.87× cash conversion.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 1.2× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 3.0% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 10% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.0× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
